title: Marubatsu 2.0

summary.en: Tic-tac-toe with one rule changed — a 4×4 board, two marks a turn — playable solo, against an AI, or online with a second phone.
summary.jp: ○×を一部変え、4×4・1 手 2 個置き。1 台でも AI 相手でも、2 台でも遊べる。

mine: Co-invented the 4×4, two-marks-per-turn rule with his son over hundreds of rounds on paper and notes apps
Built one board that works face-to-face, against an AI opponent, and online
Built the Gemini-first AI opponent with a local-search fallback across 4 difficulty levels
Wrote the QR/code pairing, presence, and rejoin logic that became the starting point for the separate Snap Pair library

challenge.en: Tic-tac-toe is solved. The first player wins or draws every time. We needed a variant that stayed recognizable — same grid concept, same win condition — but opened strategic depth without becoming chess. And it had to work solo, with an AI, or online between two phones.
challenge.jp: ○×ゲームは解決済み。先手必勝か引き分け。同じグリッド概念、同じ勝利条件を保ちながら、戦略の深みを開く変種が必要だった。そしてチェスにならずに。しかも、一人でも AI 相手でも、二台のスマホでオンラインでも動く必要があった。

solution.en: A 4×4 board where you place two marks per turn. Invented iteratively with my son on ferry rides, refined over hundreds of rounds. Gemini evaluates positions; local search backs it up. The decisive move was keeping the core recognizable while breaking the solved equilibrium.
solution.jp: 1手で2個置く 4×4 盤。息子とフェリーで反復発明し、何百局で洗練。Gemini がポジションを評価し、ローカル探索がバックアップ。決定打は、解決済みの均衡を破りながら、核を認識可能に保つこと。

_notes: Thumbnail, still and preview come from the 2026-09 screen recordings (assets/marubatsu/masters/).

cardLine.jp: 4×4 の盤で一手に二つ置く、○×ゲーム。
